study: Randel et al. (2016 / NCEE 2011-4005), CASL classroom-assessment PD, cluster RCT, REL Central, math
eval_evidence: Conducted and authored by REL Central (Mid-continent Research for Education and Learning / McREL) under the IES Regional Educational Laboratory program; authors explicitly state no financial interests in CASL. A third-party IES/REL contractor evaluating a commercially developed program (CASL by Stiggins/ATI).
developer_evidence: CASL was developed by the Assessment Training Institute (Stiggins/Chappuis), not the evaluators. PD was self-administered via textbook+DVDs and teacher learning teams; REL Central only 'provided schools... with the complete set of CASL [materials]', ran participant orientations, and provided a facilitator. The program is 'designed to be self-executing, without a coach or external facilitator', so neither the developer nor evaluator delivered ongoing PD to teachers.
cascade_evidence: Each intervention school had 'access to a facilitator who had attended a training workshop conducted by the CASL developers', who then ran the school's teacher learning teams. CASL developers -> school facilitator -> learning-team teachers = >=1 transmission hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison schools continued business-as-usual professional development (no CASL); 67 schools, 33 intervention / 34 control.
coaching_evidence: Explicitly no in-class coaching: 'The CASL program is designed to be self-executing, without a coach or external facilitator.' PD delivered through self-study and periodic teacher learning-team meetings, not classroom coaching.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention changes only teachers' classroom (formative/classroom assessment) practice; no tutoring, pull-out, added student minutes, or student-facing software dose.
maturity_evidence: Two-phase design: a CASL training year followed by an implementation year; the primary student-achievement outcome (spring 2009 CSAP) was measured at the END of the implementation year, i.e. after a prior training-year of CASL exposure for teachers.
